source.title: Otx2-PNN Interaction to Regulate Cortical Plasticity

confidence_rationale: Review-level synthesis of the canonical mechanism MECH-333 invokes: maturation of parvalbumin inhibitory interneurons (gated by Otx2 transfer and perineuronal-net assembly) triggers critical-period onset, and the same machinery controls closure. Supports the inhibitory-maturation-opens-the-window premise but is a review (not primary data), so confidence is held below the empirical entries.
failure_signatures: Critical-period onset is triggered specifically by parvalbumin-interneuron maturation and perineuronal-net consolidation; before that maturation the window does not open. A REE plasticity window keyed to a diversity/inhibitory element predicts no plasticity until that element reaches a threshold maturity -- a falsifiable timing prediction.

Perineuronal nets that consolidate around mature PV cells act to CLOSE the window and stabilize the circuit; disrupting them can reopen plasticity. The same structure that opens the window later enforces winner-take-all stabilization -- consistent with MECH-333's 'before winner-take-all capture' framing but implying the closing mechanism is an active brake, not mere decay.

mapping.source_claim_statement: In the visual cortex, critical-period onset is triggered by the maturation of parvalbumin (PV) inhibitory interneurons, which become enwrapped by perineuronal nets (PNNs); the homeoprotein Otx2 is transferred specifically into PV interneurons and this transfer regulates both the onset and the closure of the critical period for binocular vision; the Otx2-PNN interaction regulates cortical plasticity during the critical period and into adulthood.
mapping.ree_translation: MECH-333's plasticity window is explicitly the REE analog of the E/I shift and inhibitory (GABA/PV) maturation that opens biological critical periods. This review synthesizes the canonical evidence for that exact mechanism: PV-interneuron maturation as the onset trigger and PNN consolidation as the closure brake, with a molecular regulator (Otx2) controlling both ends. It supports MECH-333's choice to gate a bounded plasticity phase on the maturation of an inhibitory/diversity element, and adds the nuance that opening and closure are controlled by the SAME machinery at different maturity thresholds.
mapping.mapping_caveat: This is a review, not primary data -- it consolidates the consensus mechanism but does not itself causally test it, so it carries less independent weight than the empirical entries (Priya 2019, Huang 2015). It also concerns the molecular/structural detail (Otx2, PNNs) that has no REE analog; only the higher-level 'inhibitory maturation opens, structural consolidation closes' logic transfers. Visual-cortex binocular plasticity -> REE policy/scoring window transfer applies.
mapping.source_context: Review of rodent visual-cortex critical-period plasticity; Otx2 homeoprotein transfer into parvalbumin interneurons and perineuronal-net regulation of onset and closure.

confidence_components.notes: Source quality 0.7 reflecting review status (synthesizes strong primary literature but is not itself a causal test). Mapping fidelity 0.6: directly supports the inhibitory-maturation-opens-the-window clause central to MECH-333. Provides the canonical mechanistic backbone (PV/PNN) that Priya 2019 tests causally and Huang 2015 partially contests, so the three entries together triangulate the claim's mechanism.
